findings.title: Revelation as a revocable gift
findings.claim: Because 17:86 makes removal depend on the source's will and denies a wakil who could recover what was revealed, 17:87's mercy and great favor make continued access legible as a revocable gift; 17:85's little, given knowledge bounds any claim of possession.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries what was revealed through an emphatic conditional of source-willed removal and then names the absence of a keeper. The preceding 17:85 limits human knowledge to what was given in little measure, and the following 17:87 continues the removal sentence with an exception of mercy and great favor. Their contact changes continued access from assumed possession into source-maintained gift.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the lack of an independent custodian and the mercy that preserves access as two sides of the same conditional: the revelation remains available by gift, while human knowledge remains bounded.
findings.containment: The focus remains a conditional threat of taking away what was revealed and the absence of a wakil; the context does not say that removal occurs. The link between 17:87's exception and preservation of the revelation is an attributed inference. A live alternative reads the mercy there more narrowly as mercy toward the addressee.

epistemic.reason: The channel material is trusted, and the parallel HFT trace is legacy_unbound. Its context coordinates agree with the packet, so the shared reading is retained while the HFT contribution remains attributed.
